title: refactor(devx): share the regex-literal walk, keep the position rule a parameter
body: Fixes #15487 Two modules each answered "does a `/` here open a `RegularExpressionLiteral`?" with their own copy: a byte-identical 14-word `REGEX_AFTER_KEYWORD` set, an `IDENT_CHAR` class, and a body walk. `js-comment-mask.mjs`'s own header records what a drifting copy costs — dropping `return` from that set passes all 23 of its self-test cases and is caught only by the corpus sweep — so the copy that drifts drifts silently in exactly the direction its owner warns about. ## The choice: a FACTORY, and the line is drawn by number of right answers The split is not "shared module vs caller"; it is **how many right answers the question has**. The **WALK** — character class, backslash sequences, line-terminator refusal, flags, and the keyword set a position rule reads — has exactly one right answer, ECMA-262's. A second copy can therefore only drift. It now lives once, as `walkRegexBody` in `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, which already owns "which bytes are literal". The **POSITION RULE** has two right answers, because the consumers fail in deliberately opposite directions: a masker over-masks safely, a scanner must never skip a span it invented. It stays a parameter. **`makeRegexRecogniser({ mayBeginAt })` rather than `regexLiteralAt(src, at, { mayBeginAt })`**: `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs` calls its recogniser from fifteen places, and an option threaded through fifteen call sites is fifteen chances to pass the other consumer's rule — the drift this change exists to end, re-created one layer up. Binding it once, ```js export const regexLiteralAt = makeRegexRecogniser({ mayBeginAt: regexMayBeginAt }); ``` leaves all fifteen call sites untouched and makes "this module's rule is THIS one" a fact about the module rather than a convention its call sites have to keep. There is no default rule and omitting one throws — a default would be one of two opposite failure directions handed silently to whichever caller forgot. ## `walkRegexBody` returns an OUTCOME, not a verdict This is the part a naive extraction gets wrong, and it is measured rather than argued. An **unclosed** body is a third place the two directions part, and the card's table does not list it: - the masker over-masks to the end of the line and reads on — **198 positions on this tree, every one a JSX closing tag** (``, ``) in a `.tsx` file; - the scanner answers "not a regex at all", so it skips nothing. So the shared half returns `{ end, closed }` and each caller decides what `closed: false` means. A shared function returning only a verdict would have picked one of those two, silently, for both. Also measured while drawing the line, over the same population: `\r` / U+2028 / U+2029 inside a walked body **0**; escaped line terminator inside a body **0**; keyword-branch hits that are member names (`map.delete / 2`) **0**. The tree has no CRLF sources at all. ## ZERO behaviour change, measured on both sides The masker proof is a **differential**, not a re-run: `scanSource` at the merge base and `scanSource` on this branch, over the **same** population (the corpus sweep's own 5929 files), comparing `comment`, `literal`, `interpolation`, `maskComments` and `stripComments` byte for byte. ``` differential scanSource(BASE 5023630b1) vs scanSource(HEAD 63fb64b99) over 5929 corpus files: files whose comment/literal/interpolation/maskComments/stripComments differ: 0 flag bytes differing in total: 0 VERDICT: byte-identical on every array, every file. ``` A plain before/after snapshot of the tree would NOT have shown this: the population contains `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` itself, whose own bytes changed, so it differs for a reason that has nothing to do with behaviour. Running both implementations over one fixed population is what removes that. Gate side, byte-identical against main (`cmp -s`, all three): | reading | verdict | |:--|:--| | `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary` (normal) | byte-identical | | `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary --report` | byte-identical (86 lines) | | `check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary --self-test` | byte-identical — 322 assertions | ⚠️ The dispatch named `--sites` / `--json`; this gate has neither flag. Its site-listing reading is `--report`, which is what was captured. ## #14742's two cross-fixture cases are KEPT, and still bite Both were **ablated** rather than reasoned about. Each leg mutates, proves the mutation reached disk (anchored `grep -cF` in both directions), runs, restores with `git checkout HEAD -- `, and proves the restore by blob hash **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`. No `dist/` is involved: `node scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` resolves the source file by path, not through a package `exports`, so there is no rebuild leg to forget. | ablation | expected direction | observed | |:--|:--|:--| | A · `makeRegexRecogniser` ignores `mayBeginAt` | mask + gate red | mask EXIT=1 (`✗ NEVER-SKIP mode reads the same / as division`), gate EXIT=1 | | B · one row deleted from the new roster | floor red, naming the row | EXIT=1, 3 named failures incl. `"NEVER-SKIP mode…" ran but is not declared` | | C · the gate's rule reads `}` as a regex position | the **divergence** case reds | EXIT=1 — `the documented DIVERGENCE between the two recognisers is gone` | | D · `return` dropped from the **shared** set | see below | mask EXIT=**0**, gate EXIT=**1**, corpus EXIT=**1** | Leg D is the interesting one, and it is the card's own lesson re-measured on the consolidated copy: - `js-comment-mask --self-test` still passes — all 44 cases — exactly as its header says ("dropping `return` passes all 23 cases and is caught only by the corpus sweep"). Consolidation did not change that. - The corpus sweep still catches it, and still names the same file: `✗ comment-mask corpus sweep: 1 of 5929 files disagree … scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs fabricates=0 over-masks=17`. **The documented backstop is intact on the shared copy.** - New: the **gate's** `--self-test` now reds too — `` `return /re/` is not read as a regex `` — because the set it reads is now the masker's set. So the shared half gained a second, faster guard it did not have as two copies. Leg C and leg D each red a different one of #14742's two cases, which is why both are kept: they now assert that the two **position rules** still agree where they must and still diverge where they must. Neither is redundant. ## New self-test section, floored `js-comment-mask --self-test` gains **9 assertions driven in BOTH position modes** — one recogniser built with an over-masking rule, one with a never-skip rule, the two differing only at the character under test so nothing here goes stale when a real rule is re-argued. An assertion in one mode alone would pass on a recogniser that ignored its parameter entirely (leg A is that mutation). The section declares a **literal roster** with a floor of its own, the way the cases table does, so a deleted or renamed assertion names itself in the refusal. It does not inherit the `interpolation` section's acknowledged un-floored debt. ``` ✓ js-comment-mask self-test: 44 cases pass (23 mask/strip corpus, 12 interpolation view, 9 shared recogniser) ``` One of the nine failed on its first run — the expected closing index was mine, not the walk's; the walk was right. Fixed the expectation, not the walk. ## Verification — every exit code captured before any pipe All on the final commit `63fb64b99`, tree clean. ``` node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs EXIT=0 ✓ comment-mask corpus sweep [scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs]: 5929 files, 0 disagree, 0 unparseable, 62.0s (comparator self-test: 12 cases pass). os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 62s · waited 143s node scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs EXIT=0 node scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs --self-test EXIT=0 node scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs EXIT=0 check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary: OK — 63 unregistered code-stamping site(s), all classified; 2 awaiting a ledger entry (#8846). (byte-identical to main) node scripts/check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs --self-test EXIT=0 check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary --self-test: 10 shapes + 322 assertions OK (vocabulary + #9098 door typing) (byte-identical to main) node scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs --self-test EXIT=0 ✓ js-comment-mask self-test: 44 cases pass (23 mask/strip corpus, 12 interpolation view, 9 shared recogniser). pnpm -s check:pm-dispatch-gates EXIT=0 ✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 1402 cases pass. (no case edited) pnpm check:nul-bytes EXIT=0 pnpm lint (eslint . --no-inline-config, whole repo) EXIT=0 os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 91s · waited 400s ``` `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **32** commands for this changeset — this is the card whose blast radius is the import graph, and the derivation was re-run on the final commit and returned the same 32. **All 32 ran and all 32 exited 0.** Three needed a build first and reported `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` / exit 3 rather than a verdict — recorded as NOT MEASURED, then built and re-run to a real reading, never counted as passes: | command | first reading | after building | final | |:--|:--|:--|:--| | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:browser-reachable-entries` | exit 1, "NOT MEASURED — dist holds no bundles" | `--filter @objectstack/spec` | EXIT=0 | | `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` | exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET | `--filter @objectstack/lint` | EXIT=0 | | `pnpm check:type-check-debt` | exit 3, 29 unbuilt dependencies | whole package closure (71 tasks) | EXIT=0 — `13 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 130.3s, 143 raw tsc error(s), none above its recorded number` | `check:browser-reachable-entries` is the gate that reads `js-comment-mask.d.mts` inside a tsc program, so its green is also the check on the declarations added there. ⚠️ The derivation printed a **STALE TREE** notice: this branch is cut at `5023630b1` and `origin/main` has since moved to `615fac3a0`, across which `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` changed — not a path this PR touches. The families above were derived from this tree; CI derives them again against the merge result. `skip-changeset`: `scripts/` publishes nothing from any package. The label is set on this PR. ## Out of scope, filed separately `scripts/js-comment-mask.d.mts` declares `selfTest(): void` while the module returns `SELF_TEST_VERDICT` — the value its own CLI dispatch checks to catch a self-test that returned without printing a verdict (#13798). Same file and same class as #15398 (the missing `interpolation` field), which is open and covers only `scanSource`.
